teams.heading: Jake White questions fitness, cohesion and confidence after second-half fade against Ireland
teams.body: Fiji head coach Jake White has raised several questions after the 43-15 loss to Ireland, chiefly why the side keeps fading after the break. Ireland scored 26 unanswered second-half points, and White said Fiji had again leaked tries in the final 20 minutes. "Is that fitness? Is that time together? Is it cohesion?" he asked. Fitness, cohesion and confidence in the game plan are all to be discussed before Round 6 against Italy, with decision-making under pressure also on the list.

lead.why: A fresh Fiji Sun report of new questions White has raised about fitness, cohesion and confidence, rather than the tap-penalty call already covered.

teams.heading: Furbank, Chessum and Atkinson return from injury for All Blacks clash
teams.body: England head coach Steve Borthwick has three key men available before Saturday's clash with New Zealand. George Furbank, Ollie Chessum and Seb Atkinson were all named in the 36-man squad on Sunday, after sitting out the 78-15 win over Japan. Chessum, the vice-captain, had a shoulder problem and Atkinson a groin complaint, while Furbank, who shone in his first England appearance in two years against Australia, had a groin problem. Tighthead prop Joe Heyes said: "We'd expect the best of New Zealand every time we face them."

lead.why: A new England event: three injured key men are back in the 36-man squad for the All Blacks test.

teams.heading: Antoine Dupont invites Zinédine Zidane to Marcoussis; Zidane says it's no problem
teams.body: Antoine Dupont has invited France football head coach Zinédine Zidane to Marcoussis, the France rugby training base, to compare notes on elite-level pressure, and Zidane has accepted. The France captain said the doors were wide open and that the two sports face the same problems at the top. Zidane replied that the exchange would be interesting and that arranging it would be no problem. Finding a common date is the next hurdle; France still have two Nations Championship games, one possibly a final at Twickenham.

lead.why: A new France captain's invitation and the reply it drew, a story no other shortlist item offers, and the Avogadro, Jalibert and Marchand items were already reported.

teams.heading: Kelleher says Ireland's scrum is improving before Springboks test
teams.body: Ireland's scrum was the one consistent element of the 43-15 win over Fiji, earning four penalties, and Kelleher believes the work is paying off. Recalling last year's 24-13 Aviva defeat, when the Springboks drew six scrum penalties, he said "It was a very tough day" and that the scrum pain has at times driven the front row on. There has been no drastic overhaul, just small tweaks, Kelleher added. Ahead of Saturday's Test he hopes they'll have "enough in the tank" to do the job.

lead.why: It is a fresh Ireland story on the set piece that will decide the Springboks test, and it carries a direct Ireland player quote.

teams.heading: Quesada retains Argentina match group, recalls Pani and invites Sette for Fiji
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has kept the Argentina match group for the Fiji game, the final pool fixture, adding Lorenzo Pani back from a long injury layoff. Federico Zanandrea drops out. Davide Sette, Italy U20 captain in last week's win over France U20 in Parma, is invited to train with the squad, and Domingo Miotti is again named among the fly-halves. Italy lost 14-19 to Argentina in Genoa, and the matchday line-up is due Thursday.

lead.why: It is the freshest Italy event in the pack: a new squad list for the Fiji match, which the reader has not seen yet.

teams.heading: Scotland close on England in world rankings after Murrayfield win over Australia
teams.body: World Rugby's men's rankings, as of Sunday, leave Scotland sixth on 85.28 points, with England fifth on 86.99. Neither side moved after Sunday's 15-12 win over Australia at Murrayfield, which left Scotland more than three points clear of the Wallabies, seventh on 82.24. Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey scored the tries, with Finn Russell adding a conversion and a late penalty. Scotland remain 1.71 points behind England.

lead.why: The match report is already in the edition history, and the rankings movement is the one genuinely new Scotland item in the shortlist.

teams.heading: Jamie Roberts hails Wales' 346-tackle defence after Cardiff win over New Zealand
teams.body: Former British and Irish Lions centre Jamie Roberts, who won 94 caps for Wales, told BBC Radio 5 Live that the defence in the 35-28 win over New Zealand showed what it means to be Welsh: "That defensive set in the second half epitomised in a way what it is to be Welsh." The numbers back him up. BBC Sport reports Wales made 346 tackles, a Test record, with lock Dafydd Jenkins on 38 and Jac Morgan on 31. Roberts never managed to beat New Zealand during his own Wales career.

lead.why: The strongest new Wales item in the pack; the top-scored U19 and New Zealand-win stories have already been reported on this tab.

teams.heading: France recall Jalibert and Jelonch, Avogadro included, for Pumas test
teams.body: France have named 42 players to prepare for the Pumas, with fly-half Matthieu Jalibert back after a quadriceps injury. Flanker Anthony Jelonch returns from concussion, though whether he is used against Argentina is open, and UBB winger Hugo Avogadro joins the senior camp at Marcoussis. Toulouse's Julien Marchand is out for the rest of the Nations Championship with a thigh problem. The Pumas, who beat Italy 19-14 in Genoa, face them on Saturday at the Stade de France.

lead.why: It is the only fresh item on the shortlist, and it concerns the squad Argentina face next Saturday.

teams.heading: Les Kiss calls Murrayfield loss 'turgid' as Wallabies drop fourth straight Test
teams.body: Kiss's own description of the match, played in heavy rain, says plenty about the afternoon. Australia had little to show for the effort beyond Max Jorgensen's late try, and the numbers back that up: four straight defeats, and at least 40 points conceded in three Tests running before Murrayfield, the most recent a 45-22 loss to England at Twickenham.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones owns crushing 15-78 England defeat after Hockings red card
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones said in his post-match interview, "I take full responsibility for the result," after the 15-78 loss to England. Japan conceded 13 tries, and the damage began in the first minute, when lock Hockings was shown a yellow card for a dangerous tackle, later upgraded to red. England then ran in five tries in about 20 minutes. Japan still scored 15 points, 10 in the first half and 5 in the second.

lead.why: The only new Japan-focused item in the shortlist, and it carries the head coach's own post-match reaction to the 15-78 defeat.

teams.heading: Ben Kay recalls Twickenham box asking if All Blacks had been hacked
teams.body: England great Ben Kay, speaking on TNT Sports, said someone in his Twickenham box asked "have New Zealand been hacked?" during Saturday's game in Cardiff. Kay said he and Danny Care had expected a Welsh start followed by a New Zealand response, but "they just never showed up". Wales won 35-28, ending 73 years without beating New Zealand, and Kay called them "absolutely phenomenal".

lead.why: A new item on the defeat that puts a fresh, quotable detail about New Zealand's collapse in front of the reader, unlike the Watson reaction already run.

teams.heading: Jesse Kriel signs on in Japan to 2028 as Springboks head home
teams.body: Kriel, who has been with Yokohama Canon Eagles since 2020, is staying put, but he understands why his team-mates are leaving. "I'm also really enjoying my rugby in Japan," he told the media this week. Many of those heading home want more time with their families, he said, and he recalled Cheslin Kolbe being on FaceTime with his children every day until it became too much for him. Faf de Klerk, Malcolm Marx, Kwagga Smith and Manie Libbok have all recently signed contracts in South Africa.

lead.why: It is a fresh player storyline that is not a reaction to the France defeat, which has already been covered in earlier editions.
